recreation_brief:
1. Background: set the entire slide background to solid light gray #F2F2F2 (0-100% width and height).
2. Top strip: draw a solid white/off-white (#FFFFFF) rectangle flush with the top edge, spanning the full slide width (0-100% horizontal) and 0%-6% of slide height; it must sit above and outside the red frame drawn in step 3.
3. Red frame: draw a rectangle with no fill and a thin 1-1.5pt dark-red (#C00000) outline spanning 5%-95% of slide width and 7%-95% of slide height; round the corners slightly (radius approx. 1% of slide width, e.g., 0.05-0.1 in).
4. Title: insert one text box occupying approx. 22%-76% of slide width and 40%-58% of slide height, centered on both axes; type exactly 'Parallelization' on line 1 and 'Implementation Issues' on line 2; format both lines as bold sans-serif (Arial/Helvetica-like), dark red #C00000, approx. 40-44pt, title case, center-aligned.
5. Slide-number badge: draw one small horizontally-oriented oval approx. 5% of slide width by 7% of slide height (about 0.65 in x 0.5 in on a 16:9 slide) at approx. 88%-93% horizontal and 10%-17% vertical (top-right, just inside the red frame); fill it yellow #FFFF99 with a purple-blue #7030A0 outline approx. 1pt; center the numeral '7' inside in small dark-gray #333333 sans-serif (approx. 12-16pt).
6. Bottom bar: draw a solid black (#000000) rectangle flush with the bottom edge, spanning the full slide width (0-100% horizontal) and 96%-100% of slide height (approx. 3-4% of slide height tall).
7. Add nothing else: no bullets, no body text, no images, no charts, no equations. Do not draw the mouse cursor seen near the title in the source frame - it is a video-recording artifact, not slide content.
